gloss: despite that; even though; and yet

definitions.gloss: despite that; even though; and yet; but
definitions.explanation: A conjunction expressing that the result or situation in the second clause is contrary to what would be expected from the first clause. Often carries a tone of frustration, disappointment, or surprise.

examples.japanese: ⟦{約束|やくそく}→約束：01517_yakusoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧なのに、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来|こ}なかった→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: It was the day we had agreed on, and yet he didn't come.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日曜日|にちようび}→日曜日：00656_nichiyoubi⟧なのに、⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Even though it was Sunday, my father went to work.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天気予報|てんきよほう}→天気予報：01678_tenkiyohou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{晴|は}れ→晴れ：02936_hare⟧だった。なのに、⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{降|ふ}っている→降る：00839_furu⟧。
examples.english: The forecast said it would be sunny. And yet it's been raining since morning.

notes:
Formed from な (the copula/na-adjective connector) + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (despite). Attaches to nouns and na-adjective stems. Very common in spoken Japanese, often expressing the speaker's frustration or complaint that reality did not match expectations.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- After nouns: ⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧なのに (despite being a student)
- After na-adjectives: ⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧なのに (despite being quiet)
- Sentence-final use: ...なのに。(expressing frustration without completing the thought)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: despite — the broader particle; なのに is specifically the noun/na-adjective form
- けど / ⟦けれど→けれど：01990_keredo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧: but — more neutral, less emotional than なのに
- ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧なのに: despite that — a longer, more emphatic version used at the start of a new sentence
- にもかかわらず: despite / in spite of — more formal written equivalent

REGISTER:
Casual to neutral. Very common in everyday spoken Japanese. The emotional nuance makes it less suitable for formal writing, where にもかかわらず is preferred.

USAGE:
When used at the end of a sentence (e.g., ⟦{日曜日|にちようび}→日曜日：00656_nichiyoubi⟧なのに...), the speaker leaves the complaint implied, creating a tone of disappointment or resignation.
